paragraphs: Our Thursday Timetable, posted by Lily. Grace, my pen pal, asked about our school day in her email. "What is a weekday like at your school?" she wrote. Today is Thursday, so this is my answer. Here is our timetable on a normal Thursday. The school day is long, but I like it.

Eight o'clock: English. Nine o'clock: math. Ten o'clock: break. Half past ten: history. Twelve o'clock: lunch. One o'clock: the Explorers club in the library. Two o'clock: science. Three o'clock: the school day ends. Nobody forgets lunch, of course. The timetable is on the wall next to the door. We read it every morning, because we want to know our lessons.

History is my favorite lesson on Thursday. Today, Teacher Kim brought an enormous map, and it almost touched the ceiling. It showed our old town many years ago. The map was so big that everybody looked up. We looked at the map and found the old market, the school, and the river. "Open your textbook at page twelve," said Teacher Kim. Leo looked in his bag, but he could not find it. "I think that I lost it on the bus," he said. Mia and I shared our textbooks with him.

After lunch, Mia and I went to the club in the library. Leo came, too, and he told Teacher Kim about the lost book. "I will ask the bus driver tomorrow," said Teacher Kim. We planned our next trip, and Mia made a list. Then Teacher Kim opened her big notebook. "I keep a record of all our homework in it," she said. We have a test on Friday, so we have homework tonight. I must read three pages of history and do ten questions of math. I will do my homework at the kitchen table, and Mom will check it.

I like our Thursday timetable, because it has many different lessons. Every lesson is different, so I never feel bored. Grace, I hope that you like it, too. Which lesson do you like best? Please write to me soon!
